question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(200,0.4),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X>90).$ Give your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.4\,$ | $\,0.9192\,$ | $\,0.9207\,$ | $\,0.9222\,$ |
| $\,1.5\,$ | $\,0.9332\,$ | $\,0.9345\,$ | $\,0.9357\,$ |
| $\,1.6\,$ | $\,0.9452\,$ | $\,0.9463\,$ | $\,0.9474\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=200$ and $p=0.4.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =200\cdot 0.4 \\  & =80 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =200\cdot (1-0.4) \\  & =120 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(200)(0.4)=80
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(200)(0.4)(1-0.4)=48.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(80,48).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X>90).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X>90)=P(X\ge 91)≈P(Y>90.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>90.5) & =P(Z>\frac{90.5-80}{\sqrt{48}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.52) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 1.52) \\  & =1-Φ(1.52) \\  & =1-0.9357 \\  & =0.0643\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X>90)≈0.064.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0648.$
